subject: mathematics
question_text: If p₁, p₂, p₃ are the altitudes of a △ABC, then show that (i) 1/p₁ + 1/p₂ + 1/p₃ = 1/r, (ii) 1/p₁ + 1/p₂ − 1/p₃ = 1/r₃, and (iii) p₁p₂p₃ = (abc)²/(8R³) = 8Δ³/(abc).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.49 — LAQ chapter 6 Properties of Triangles, answer 39. Printed appearances: TS 18. THREE results from one setup. All three follow from a single observation — each altitude is 2Δ divided by its own base — so that is established once and then used three times. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print a full 1×7 split against answer 32 on book p.44, so the granularity is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow the natural steps. The book's chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '7 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q24 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q17 (SAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other. FIGURE: the book prints one against this answer — triangle ABC with the altitude from A dropped onto BC, its right angle marked and the base named a (book p.49). It is the ONLY figure in the Properties of Triangles chapter, and it is redrawn as its own step because pairing each altitude with the side it is dropped onto is what all three parts rest on. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to the "Prove part (iii)" step.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Express each altitude
steps.margin_note: Two marks, and the whole setup. The area can be computed from any side and its altitude, so Δ = ½ a p₁ — which rearranges to p₁ = 2Δ/a. The other two follow by symmetry.
steps.memory_tip: Area from any side and its own height: Δ = ½ a p₁, so p₁ = 2Δ/a. The other two follow by symmetry.
lines: p₁ is the altitude from A to BC, so
Δ = ½ (base)(height) = ½ (BC)(p₁) = ½ a p₁

recall.must_convey: That Δ = ½ a p₁ gives p₁ = 2Δ/a, so 1/p₁ = a/(2Δ), and similarly for the others.
accept: the area is half base times height so p one is two delta over a and its reciprocal is a over two delta
each altitude is twice the area divided by its own base
one over p one is a over two delta
delta equals half a p one, so p one equals two delta by a
express the altitudes using the area

steps.why: Taking the RECIPROCALS is what makes all three parts easy — 1/p is a simple multiple of the side, where p itself is a fraction.
common_mistakes: Pairing p₁ with the wrong side.

steps.label: Draw the triangle
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark but worth drawing. The altitude p₁ is the HEIGHT onto BC, and BC is the base a — the picture is what pairs each altitude with the side it is dropped onto, which is the whole content of Δ = ½ a p₁.
steps.memory_tip: The picture pairs each altitude with the side it is dropped onto — that pairing is the whole content.

recall.must_convey: That triangle ABC is sketched with the altitude from A drawn onto BC, its right angle marked and the base named a. Naming the drawing is full credit — it cannot be spoken.
accept: draw the triangle and drop the altitude from A onto BC
sketch A B C and mark p one as the height on side a
show the perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side
triangle geesi A nunchi BC meeda altitude veyyali
draw the triangle with its altitude

steps.why: Every one of the three parts starts from the same area statement, and that statement only reads correctly off a picture: p₁ is the height ONLY when BC is the base. Drawing it once fixes all three pairings — p₁ with a, p₂ with b, p₃ with c.
common_mistakes: Pairing p₁ with the wrong side, which breaks all three results at once.
Treating the altitude as a median — it meets BC at a right angle, not at its midpoint.

steps.label: Prove part (i)
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The three reciprocals share 1/(2Δ), and a + b + c is 2s — so the sum becomes s/Δ, which is 1/r.
steps.memory_tip: The three reciprocals share 1/(2Δ), and a + b + c = 2s, so the sum is s/Δ = 1/r.

recall.must_convey: That the three reciprocals sum to (a+b+c)/(2Δ) = s/Δ = 1/r.
accept: add the reciprocals to get a plus b plus c over two delta which is s over delta which is one over r
the sum is s over delta and r is delta over s so it is one over r
it comes to one over the in radius
a plus b plus c two s kabatti s by delta, ante one by r
the sum of the reciprocals is one over r

steps.why: r = Δ/s, so 1/r = s/Δ. Recognising the answer as a reciprocal rather than deriving it fresh is what makes this two lines.

steps.label: Prove part (ii)
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. The same sum with a minus on the third: a + b − c is 2s − 2c = 2(s−c), and Δ/(s−c) is r₃.
steps.memory_tip: With a minus on the third: a + b − c = 2s − 2c = 2(s − c), and Δ/(s − c) is r₃.

recall.must_convey: That a + b − c = 2(s−c), so the expression is (s−c)/Δ = 1/r₃.
accept: a plus b minus c is two s minus two c so it becomes s minus c over delta which is one over r three
add and subtract two c to reach two s minus two c
the answer is one over r three
a plus b minus c ante two s minus two c, so one by r three
the minus gives the third ex radius

steps.why: Writing a + b − c as a + b + c − 2c is the trick — it turns an awkward combination into 2s minus something, which is what the ex-radius formula needs.
common_mistakes: Pairing the minus with r₁ instead of r₃.

steps.label: Prove part (iii)
steps.margin_note: Last two marks. Multiply the three altitudes, then convert using abc = 4RΔ to reach the second form.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply the three altitudes, then convert using abc = 4RΔ to reach the second form.

recall.must_convey: That the product is 8Δ³/(abc), and substituting Δ = abc/(4R) converts it to (abc)²/(8R³).
accept: multiply the three altitudes to get eight delta cubed over a b c then substitute delta to get a b c squared over eight R cubed
the product is eight delta cubed over abc
use delta equals abc over four R to get the other form
moodintini multiply cheste eight delta cube by abc vasthundi
both forms of the answer follow

steps.why: The question asked for BOTH forms, so the conversion is required, not optional. R = abc/(4Δ) rearranges to give Δ, which is what makes the swap possible.
common_mistakes: Giving only one of the two forms.

insider_note: Everything follows from p₁ = 2Δ/a, so write that first and the three parts become arithmetic. Part (ii) needs a + b − c = 2s − 2c, which is where the (s−c) comes from.
